subject: On-prem VPC landing interfaces and control/data-plane review
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@edgeops.io>, EdgeOps Networking <networking@edgeops.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem VPC landing interfaces and control/data-plane review

Tom / EdgeOps team —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is the landing-zone sketch (PDF) and the interface matrix (XLSX) that I promised. We want to lock in the control-plane connectivity pattern and the minimal egress/peering requirements for the PoC so we can move to wiring and test credentials next week. High-level asks: 

- Confirm whether you can accept a private peering (Direct Connect/Partner interconnect) into the customer VPC for control-plane RPCs and telemetry.
- Confirm NAT/egress constraints for data-plane worker nodes (do they allow outbound to a small set of Redwood egress IPs, or is private peering required for data egress as well?).
- Review the proposed interface ports (see sheet "ports") and tell us any blocked ports/policy constraints.

Summary of the proposed pattern in the docs: control-plane components (orchestration, shipper, registries) sit logically in the customer VPC in a dedicated subnet with an internal NLB in front of the control API. Mutual TLS between Redwood control-plane clients and customer-facing control-plane endpoint; traffic restricted to the peered network. Data-plane nodes (in customer racks) reach out for model artifacts over HTTPS and stream inference traffic to Redwood-managed egress proxies in the same region when private peering is not available.

If you can annotate the PDF with required changes and return the matrix with any blocked ports, we’ll produce an updated wiring diagram and a short runbook for the PoC hardware lead.

Available times for a quick follow-up: Tue 26th 10–11am PT or Wed 27th 2–4pm PT.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: landing_zone_sketch_v2.pdf (diagram), interface_matrix_v3.xlsx (ports + ACLs)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@edgeops.io>, EdgeOps Networking <networking@edgeops.io>
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC landing interfaces and control/data-plane review

Jordan / team —

Quick technical notes after going through the sketch and matrix:

- Control-plane placement: we should avoid exposing any public control-plane endpoints. The internal NLB pattern is fine; prefer a dual-AZ NLB in front of an auto-scaling control-plane fleet with sticky TLS sessions disabled.
- Auth: mutual TLS + client cert whitelisting per customer is required for our SLA customers. We'll provision a unique client cert for EdgeOps PoC.
- Ports: for the control API we only need TCP 8443 (control API) and 9090 for health/metrics if you want remote scraping. If the customer security team insists on blocking 9090, we can push metrics via a secure webhook to a collector in their network instead.
- NAT / egress: data-plane nodes must be allowed outbound HTTPS (443) to the artifact registry (S3-style endpoint) and outbound to our egress proxy pool for model telemetry. If private peering is possible for egress, we can avoid opening any internet egress at all and route model pulls over the interconnect.
- Telemetry: prefer a dedicated telemetry subnet for sFlow/metrics over TLS; avoid mixing telemetry with control plane in the same endpoint.

One caution: if the customer's on-prem NAT translates many hosts to a single IP, we lose per-node observability for billing/telemetry. If the customer can provide SNAT exemption for worker nodes to a small IP range that will help.

I'll attach a brief port summary and a proposed minimal firewall ACL in the matrix.

Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachment referenced: interface_matrix_v3.xlsx

From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@edgeops.io>

Cc: EdgeOps Networking <networking@edgeops.io>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC landing interfaces and control/data-plane review

Jordan / Marcus / team —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few constraints from our side: 

- We cannot expose any control-plane endpoints to the public internet for this customer (sensitive regulated workload). Private peering into the customer VPC is strongly preferred.
- The on-prem team will not allow a global SNAT that collapses all worker nodes into a single IP for the initial PoC. We can allocate a /28 SNAT pool for the cluster egress which should give you per-node visibility.
- Ports: TCP 8443 for control-plane is fine. We will block port 9090 for metrics but can accept push-based metrics to our collector if you provide the endpoint.
- We can stand up a private Direct Connect via our carrier partner, but it will take 7–10 business days to provision. If you need a faster path, we can temporary provision a VPN tunnel over the partner circuit and convert to DX later.

Action items on our side: provide the exact peer ASN, BGP prefixes, and the NLB internal IP proposal by EOD Friday so our network team can start the circuit ticket. For the PoC we can do private peering for both control-plane and egress if Redwood can accept the /28 SNAT range for billing/observability.

We can do a follow-up call Thursday 28th 11am PT to confirm the ACL sheet.

—Tom
Tom Reilly
Network Architect, EdgeOps Inc.
tom.reilly@edgeops.io
+1 (206) 555-0147

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@edgeops.io>, EdgeOps Networking <networking@edgeops.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC landing interfaces and control/data-plane review — decisions & next steps

Tom / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the SNAT commitment. Summary of decisions from our side and next steps for the PoC: 

Decisions agreed
- Control-plane will be provisioned in the customer VPC behind an internal NLB. No public control-plane endpoints.
- Mutual TLS for control-plane traffic; Redwood will generate a client certificate for EdgeOps PoC use.
- Data-plane egress: use the customer-provided /28 SNAT range for PoC. If long term they prefer private peering for model pulls, we will switch to the interconnect path in parallel.
- Metrics: we will switch to push-based telemetry to your collector endpoint (TLS).

Next steps
- Jordan to upload updated interface_matrix_v3.xlsx with explicit peer ASN, BGP prefixes, and NLB internal IP suggestions (by EOD Friday) — action: jordan_blake.
- EdgeOps to open circuit ticket and share provisioning ETA; provide VPN fallback timeline if DX delayed — action: tom.reilly@edgeops.io.
- Marcus / Karthik to produce a short PoC runbook (wiring steps, cert exchange, smoke tests) — action: marcus_lin, karthik_iyer.

If there are any items missing or you want a different run cadence, let me know. If this looks good, please reply with a one-line ACK and we’ll lock the circuit info into the matrix.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: interface_matrix_v3.xlsx (updated with peer ASN placeholder)
